In 2019, our state banned mental health professionals from practicing ineffective (and often, significantly harmful) conversion therapy with LGBTQ+ clients under 18 years of age.

But, friend, I'm seriously concerned that could soon change.
Last week, the Supreme Court heard arguments in a case that could overturn Colorado's law – and this isn't your typical Supreme Court.
In case after case, the majority has been all too eager to advance an ultraconservative political and cultural agenda at the expense of our democratic guardrails and civil rights.

body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTMwNjkzNDUS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjMyMDgzNzAxNwS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter — earlier this week we shared a bombshell update: in the midst of
the government shutdown, Trump is rushing approval of the Ambler Road Project, a
200 mile roadway that would open Alaska's wilderness to destructive mining
operations. The response has been humbling — folks from all over the country have pitched
into our campaign to fight back, renewing their LCV memberships, and getting
their contributions triple matched. We’re reaching out today because we haven’t heard back from you yet, Peter — and this is an important one. Can you renew your membership before our campaign deadline? Right now, $5 is all it takes. Just click here to TRIPLE your impact >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thanks for your support. See our message from earlier this week for more details
— the stakes couldn’t be higher. — LCV Membership Team DEVELOPING... despite the ongoing government shutdown, Trump has quietly deemed the
permitting process for polluters “essential” — and just ordered the approval of
over 200 miles of roadway opening Alaska’s wilderness to destructive mining. The proposed Ambler Road Project is opposed by Alaska Native communities and
would greenlight the destruction of hundreds of miles of wilderness. It
threatens permanent devastation for Alaskan ecosystems and wildlife, all to
benefit foreign mining interests. The environmental implications are horrible. And, this speculative project would
compete against existing mines that cannot run economically — threatening to
despoil this unique wilderness and then go belly up, leaving taxpayers and local
Alaskans with the cleanup costs and toxic legacy. We can’t let Trump speculate with our public lands just because he got cozy with
their executives. The environmental movement is mobilizing to stop this project,but we need YOUR help. Right now, there’s an incredible opportunity to power the
resistance to Trump’s dirty agenda — a group of donors will TRIPLE MATCH all
gifts up to $50,000 until October 31. The best thing you can do right now to fight for the environment is to renew your LCV membership. Right now, $5 is all it takes to renew >> https://links.messages.lcv. The proposed Ambler Road Project would cross more than 3,000 streams and riversover 200 miles in a part of Alaska that is important for subsistence and
wildlife, and it would threaten water sources and fisheries with toxic
contamination. This is just the latest example of Trump continuing to sell off our public lands
to corporationsin order to serve the interests of his billionaire buddies in the fossil fuel,
logging, and mining industries. It’s corruption, plain and simple: while government services and federal lands
remain closed to ordinary Americans, the White House remains open for business
to serve Trump’s corporate cronies. Peter, Trump may have these billionaires in his back pocket, but we
have something even more powerful in our corner: we have YOU and a community of
people who care about our environment. Because this fight is so important, a
group of donors will TRIPLE your impact when you renew your LCV membership
before October 31. Please don’t wait: renew your membership for just $5 to TRIPLE your impact >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thanks for everything you do for the environment, Peter. Chris Brooks

name: Heidi Hall
subject: Grass Valley taught me so much
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY HEIDI HALL FOR CONGRESS
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20251016_em_fr_b1_HH_standard [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20251016_em_fr_b1_HH_standard]
Friend,
From my childhood to today, Grass Valley and our small rural communities have taught me so much.
When I was growing up in the Bay Area, I would spend my summers with my grandparents and scoop ice cream to make some extra money. It was during those times that I learned that while a lot of things may seem different, they're actually the same.
My time in the EPA only reinforced that belief, and as I interacted with different tribal, local, state, and federal governments, I remembered Grass Valley and how everyone was looking for the same thing— a better future.
Friend, I'm constantly learning from the conversations that I have with people in our district, and if there's one more thing that I've learned from our rural communities, it's that Kevin Kiley doesn't understand us at all.
We don't need a careerist in Congress who will vote to cut Medicaid and SNAP spending—we need someone who will listen.

body:
CIA’s Jeffrey Epstein Records

[INSIDE JW]

THE SUPREME COURT MUST END ILLEGAL VOTE COUNTING

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77249&L=36305&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1jRm1tWnAzd0tLWSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=ecc38613f703c078eb691b584bcf0ec01a829e95869b8b460d31cc9be1df7517]

In my op-ed
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77249&L=36306&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2FzaGluZ3RvbnRpbWVzLmNvbS9uZXdzLzIwMjUvb2N0LzE1L3N1cHJlbWUtY291cnQtbXVzdC1lbmQtaWxsZWdhbC12b3RlLWNvdW50aW5nLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=650676fca48cdd3d34b5e66f7ad264b8c02df33162c862cfd1f1c0be09ee2107]
for _The Washington Times _this week, I write that ballot tallying
must conclude on Election Day:

> Under federal law, Election Day in the United States is not two
> days, two weeks or two months. It is a single day. That anyone might
> insist otherwise is difficult to imagine.
>
> Last week, the Supreme Court
>
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77249&L=36307&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2FzaGluZ3RvbnRpbWVzLmNvbS90b3BpY3Mvc3VwcmVtZS1jb3VydC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=214afd0069e83bf4fd47ce5a6334e39810c763a4bbc66f1b440297b71c960ea2]
heard oral
> arguments in _Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections_, a case
> challenging Illinois’ decision to count mail-in-ballots that
> arrive up to 14 days after Election Day. For 180 years, Election Day
> has been held on the same day in November. This date has been
> repeatedly reaffirmed by Congress and solidified into U.S. law. Yet
> in 2005, in flagrant violation of that law, Illinois began
> permitting the counting of mail-in ballots received up to 14 days
> after Election Day.
>
> It should be deeply concerning that in 2020 alone, Illinois received
> 4.4% of votes from November 3 to November 17, after Election Day.
>
> Fortunately, U.S. Rep. Mike Bost of Illinois and two Republican
> state presidential electors decided to challenge this policy in the
> courts, represented by my organization, Judicial Watch. They began
> by suing Illinois in May 2022.
>
> Their case should have been easy to decide, but shockingly, the U.S.
> District Court for the Northern District of Illinois and the 7th
> U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that neither Mr. Bost nor the
> electors had “standing” to bring the lawsuit. In short, the
> courts refused even to permit the plaintiffs a chance to challenge
> the counting of late ballots in court.
>
> That question has reached the Supreme Court
>
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=77249&L=36307&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud2FzaGluZ3RvbnRpbWVzLmNvbS90b3BpY3Mvc3VwcmVtZS1jb3VydC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=214afd0069e83bf4fd47ce5a6334e39810c763a4bbc66f1b440297b71c960ea2],
and the
> justices showed serious skepticism toward Illinois’ defense.
>
> Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. questioned whether the state’s
> position would force courts to step into election disputes “at the
> most fraught time” in electoral politics. He pressed the Illinois
> solicitor general on why a candidate should have to wait until an
> election’s outcome is uncertain to challenge an unlawful rule.
>
> Justice Brett M. Kavanaugh added that such a theory “depends on
> prognostication,” not law. Justice Neil M. Gorsuch warned that it
> would be “unseemly” for courts to predict a candidate’s
> chances of winning, a process that “itself might influence the
> election.”
>
> As Judicial Watch attorney Paul Clement argued to the judges,
> “candidates have standing to challenge the rules that govern the
> election.”
>
> Spending additional money and time to deal with illicit vote
> counting should be more than enough to give a candidate his day in
> court. Allowing late ballots to be counted extends Election Day for
> weeks and imposes significant and burdensome costs on candidates,
> who will be forced to extend campaigns well beyond the usual time
> frame. Candidates will also be required to foot the bill for
> representatives to oversee the counting of late-arriving ballots.
>
> Voters rightly expect prompt results after the democratic process of
> casting ballots. Voter confidence in election outcomes suffers when
> winners and losers are not promptly announced. If Americans do not
> have confidence in the results of our elections, our entire system
> of government is imperiled. The court’s decision in Bost will
> determine whether candidates, those directly governed by election
> rules, can defend the rule of law before Election Day chaos unfolds.
>
> If the justices rule for Mr. Bost, lower courts will finally have to
> judge Illinois’ 14-day counting window against the federal statute
> requiring a single, uniform Election Day. That could set a
> nationwide precedent, restoring the integrity of vote counting in
> every state.
>
> We should hear [very soon] whether the Supreme Court will take up a
> Mississippi case where the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled
> that Mississippi cannot count ballots after Election Day.
>
> All Americans deserve a system of integrity and transparency, not
> one that invites fraud and election rigging. The 5th Circuit has
> already agreed with Judicial Watch that counting ballots even five
> days after Election Day is unlawful. If the Supreme Court now
> confirms that principle and rules in our clients’ favor, we like
> the odds of ending this illicit vote counting in Illinois and across
> the nation.

clean_body: CIA’s Jeffrey Epstein Records [INSIDE JW] THE SUPREME COURT MUST END ILLEGAL VOTE COUNTING [] In my op-ed [] for The Washington Times this week, I write that ballot tallying must conclude on Election Day: Under federal law, Election Day in the United States is not two days, two weeks or two months. It is a single day. That anyone might insist otherwise is difficult to imagine. Last week, the Supreme Court [] heard oral arguments in Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections, a case challenging Illinois’ decision to count mail-in-ballots that arrive up to 14 days after Election Day. For 180 years, Election Day has been held on the same day in November. This date has been repeatedly reaffirmed by Congress and solidified into U.S. law. Yet in 2005, in flagrant violation of that law, Illinois began permitting the counting of mail-in ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day. It should be deeply concerning that in 2020 alone, Illinois received 4.4% of votes from November 3 to November 17, after Election Day. Fortunately, U.S. Rep. Mike Bost of Illinois and two Republican state presidential electors decided to challenge this policy in the courts, represented by my organization, Judicial Watch. They began by suing Illinois in May 2022. Their case should have been easy to decide, but shockingly, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois and the 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that neither Mr. Bost nor the electors had “standing” to bring the lawsuit. In short, the courts refused even to permit the plaintiffs a chance to challenge the counting of late ballots in court. That question has reached the Supreme Court [], and the justices showed serious skepticism toward Illinois’ defense. Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. questioned whether the state’s position would force courts to step into election disputes “at the most fraught time” in electoral politics. He pressed the Illinois solicitor general on why a candidate should have to wait until an election’s outcome is uncertain to challenge an unlawful rule. Justice Brett M. Kavanaugh added that such a theory “depends on prognostication,” not law. Justice Neil M. Gorsuch warned that it would be “unseemly” for courts to predict a candidate’s chances of winning, a process that “itself might influence the election.” As Judicial Watch attorney Paul Clement argued to the judges, “candidates have standing to challenge the rules that govern the election.” Spending additional money and time to deal with illicit vote counting should be more than enough to give a candidate his day in court. Allowing late ballots to be counted extends Election Day for weeks and imposes significant and burdensome costs on candidates, who will be forced to extend campaigns well beyond the usual time frame. Candidates will also be required to foot the bill for representatives to oversee the counting of late-arriving ballots. Voters rightly expect prompt results after the democratic process of casting ballots. Voter confidence in election outcomes suffers when winners and losers are not promptly announced. If Americans do not have confidence in the results of our elections, our entire system of government is imperiled. The court’s decision in Bost will determine whether candidates, those directly governed by election rules, can defend the rule of law before Election Day chaos unfolds. If the justices rule for Mr. Bost, lower courts will finally have to judge Illinois’ 14-day counting window against the federal statute requiring a single, uniform Election Day. That could set a nationwide precedent, restoring the integrity of vote counting in every state. We should hear [very soon] whether the Supreme Court will take up a Mississippi case where the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Mississippi cannot count ballots after Election Day. All Americans deserve a system of integrity and transparency, not one that invites fraud and election rigging. The 5th Circuit has already agreed with Judicial Watch that counting ballots even five days after Election Day is unlawful. If the Supreme Court now confirms that principle and rules in our clients’ favor, we like the odds of ending this illicit vote counting in Illinois and across the nation. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES CIA FOR JEFFREY EPSTEIN RECORDS We went back to court in our effort to uncover what our government knows about registered sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) for records involving any role Jeffrey Epstein might have played in connection with the agency, his business dealings, travel, victim or witness information, and records concerning his death (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Central Intelligence Agency [] (No. 1:25-cv-03618)). We sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after the CIA failed to respond to a July 9, 2025, FOIA request for: Intelligence activities and connections, including any records indicating whether Epstein was ever an asset for any U.S. or foreign intelligence agency and/or reports analyzing his potential connections to foreign intelligence services. Financial and business activities, including analyses concerning Epstein’s wealth accumulation, estimated at approximately $560 million at the time of his 2019 arrest. Associations and networks, including records documenting Epstein’s interactions with high-profile executives, royalty, or other prominent figures, where such interactions were of interest to the CIA due to national security concerns. Also, records about his so-called “Black Book” or contact lists, as well as his properties that may have been referenced in CIA reports. Criminal investigations and legal proceedings, including records about coordination with other federal agencies, such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Department of Justice (DOJ), or U.S. Marshals Service, regarding Epstein’s criminal activities. Also, records about his death in 2019 at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York. Surveillance and evidence collection. Foreign connections and travel. * Victim and witness information. In May 2023, Epstein was reported [] to have met “dozens of times” with former Israel Prime Minister Ehud Barak between 2013-2017. Epstein reportedly donated [] $110,000 to former U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers wife’s online poetry project in 2016 and held meetings with many other high profile individuals “long after he was a registered sex offender. He had pleaded guilty in 2008 [] to soliciting and procuring a minor for prostitution.” Attorney General Pamela Bondi released a long-awaited [] [ of documents related to Epstein in February 2025, but “the much-hyped, roughly 200-page document dump provided no big revelations, instead listing celebrities and politicians who were already known to have palled around with the notorious pedophile.” America’s federal intelligence and law enforcement agencies need to obey the law and provide some basic information about Jeffrey Epstein. Our FOIA lawsuits for records are an important step toward accountability. In April 2025, we filed a related lawsuit [] against the U.S. Department of Justice after it failed to adequately respond to four separate FOIA requests for records regarding Epstein, including any records on the identities of his clients or associates. In July, the Justice Department reported to the court [] that it and the FBI were continuing to search for and review responsive records. The Justice Department’s disclosure is at odds with the leaked, unsigned and undated Justice Department/FBI memo [] that suggests no more Epstein records would be disclosed to the American public. The memo was first disclosed late on July 6 []. In July 2025, we sued [] the Justice Department for all interviews, conversations and other records provided to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) by Epstein victim Virginia Louise Giuffre, who reportedly [] committed suicide on April 25, 2025. JUDGE RULES PRISON MUST GRANT SEX-CHANGE SURGERY FOR SERIAL CHILD MOLESTER Our courts are making gender surgery a constitutional right, as our Corruption Chronicles blog reports []. The state prison system, where a convicted serial child molester is serving a 40-year sentence for sexually abusing multiple kids over a decade, is violating the felon’s constitutional rights by refusing to provide him with costly genital surgery to treat his gender dysphoria, a federal judge has determined. The transgender inmate, Emalee Wagoner, was arrested in 2011 and charged with 50 counts of sexually abusing several children, including his stepchildren, biological daughter, and the daughter of a family friend throughout a 10-year period. He threatened to kill his underage victims if they told anyone about the pervasive abuse, official court documents reveal. In 2015 Wagoner pled guilty and was sentenced to 60 years in prison with 20 years suspended. At some point during his incarceration in Alaska the child molester began identifying as a woman and a few years ago started undergoing hormone therapy. He was subsequently diagnosed with gender dysphoria, a condition in which people reportedly experience distress because their gender identity differs from their biological sex. Alaska has a policy of locking up convicts based on sex assigned at birth, so Wagoner is serving time at a medium-security men’s prison called Goose Creek Correctional Center in Wasilla about 40 miles north of Anchorage. For several years the convicted child predator has been trying to get the Alaska Department of Corrections (DOC) to provide him with gender-affirming surgery to become a woman, but the state has refused after the DOC medical advisory committee determined there was insufficient evidence to affirm the inmate’s mental health and well-being will decline without the procedure. Wagoner’s attorney, who works for a nonprofit dedicated to promoting and litigating on behalf of LGBTQ+ rights, says gender-affirming surgery should be considered at the same level as cancer treatment [] [ that if a prisoner needs it, they can immediately get it. According to court documents [], Wagoner started to “socially transition” while in prison in 2016, changing his external presentation by growing out his hair, changing his name, wearing makeup and otherwise presenting as female to the extent possible. The Alaska DOC subsequently confirmed the diagnosis of gender dysphoria and shortly later Wagoner tried to perform a “penile inversion surgery to create a neo-vagina on herself.” The child sexual predator continues to crush his testicles, the legal filing reveals, and receives women’s deodorant and cosmetics, feminine hair accessories, and styling instruments as well as women’s undergarments. State officials have clearly made efforts to accommodate the transgender inmate but drew the line at surgery, so he sued the prison system. It is not the first time a federal court determines that denying a sex-change operation violates the Constitution. Last year an Obama-appointed judge ruled [] that the U.S. military’s health insurance plan is discriminatory and violates Equal Protection rights under the Fifth Amendment of the U.S. Constitution by failing to cover gender transition surgeries. The ruling was issued after two transgender women sued the Department of Defense (DOD) and its Tricare Health Plan over a provision that bans surgical coverage of procedures that improve physical appearance without a significant restoration of functions, including “sex gender changes.” The biological males, who want to be female, claim in their lawsuit that denying coverage of medically necessary gender transition surgeries violates their Constitutional Equal Protection rights, a guarantee that requires the government “to treat alike all persons similarly situated.” Until next week, [Contribute] [] [32x32x1] [] [32x32x2] [] [32x32x3] [] [32x32x3] [] Judicial Watch, Inc. 425 3rd St Sw Ste 800 Washington, DC 20024 202.646.5172 © 2017 - 2025, All Rights Reserved Manage Email Subscriptions [] |

Peter,

The radical left thinks they can dismiss us, calling us**“backward,” “extreme,”** and worse. They’re attacking the Minnesota values I’ve spent a lifetime defending — faith, family, and freedom. But here’s the truth they don’t want you to know: we’re closer than ever to taking back this Senate seat.

With the election fast approaching, _**attention is turning to Minnesota’s Senate race.**_ My opponents, Tim Walz’s lieutenant governor, Peggy Flanagan, and Rep. subject: A personal story about my health
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=em20251017-1123&t=1001&akid=1126%2E251025%2Ev7tvf_ ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=em20251017-1123&t=1002&akid=1126%2E251025%2Ev7tvf_ ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

I’ll be honest with you. In a moment, I’m going to ask for your support.
But first, I’d like to share a personal story about my health.

Thanks for taking a minute of your time to read. 🙏

A few years ago, I started to feel a heaviness around the lower right side
of my abdomen while lifting weights. Having gone to medical school, I knew
that the pressure I was feeling was likely a hernia, which about 30% of
men develop at some point in their lives.

Luckily, I wasn’t in pain, but I knew that if left untreated, there was a
chance it could develop into a potentially deadly condition.

To treat or not to treat? It should’ve been an easy decision.

However, the surgery required to heal my condition would cost several
thousand dollars, and that’s *with* insurance.

Ultimately, I decided I’d undergo the surgery. But had I not been insured
or able to cover my out-of-pocket costs, I would’ve been left with no
choice but to take on thousands in medical debt or ignore a hole in my
abdominal wall that could eventually kill me.

This is a tragically common problem under our broken healthcare system.

Peter, you and
most people reading this email have probably personally endured, or know
someone who’s endured, this same dilemma.

Medical debt is the leading cause of bankruptcy in this country, and it’s
a symptom of the broken, diseased system under which healthcare executives
get richer while the rest of us are forced into debt simply to stay alive.

The reason I’m sharing this story isn’t to prove how much I know about
hernias — or even to subtly mention that I lift!

I share this because I believe you shouldn’t have to win the lottery of
life to succeed in this country, the richest nation in the history of the
world.

I’m running for U.S. Senate because it’s long past time to change the
system that makes wealth the defining factor in whether you can build a
good, healthy life for your family.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20251017-1-ak.PVPsbD&amount=10&refcode=em20251017-1123&t=1004&akid=1126%2E251025%2Ev7tvf_ ]If you’re with me, please donate $10 today. Together,
we’ll fight for Medicare for All and a government that actually supports
working people.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

body:
From a single working mom to Congresswoman and Secretary of the Interior — and now with your help, Governor of New Mexico.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=5115%2E400544%2EQOVF8W)
Before I ever thought about running for office, I was a single mom living paycheck to paycheck.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251017_1_singlemom.N0BOaB&amount=5&%3Brefcode=em20251017-5115&t=2&akid=5115%2E400544%2EQOVF8W)
Balancing work and parenting was not easy. There were times I didn’t know how we would make ends meet. Thankfully, programs like SNAP and Medicaid were there for us when we needed them.
**But Donald Trump and Republicans are gutting them, along with other vital lifelines, making it even harder for working families to build a better life.**
**[Democratic governors are on the frontlines of this fight — and New Mexico needs a leader who understands what’s at stake and will fight fiercely to protect working families. If you’re with me, will you chip in $5 to help me win this wide-open seat?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251017_1_singlemom.N0BOaB&amount=5&refcode=em20251017-5115&t=3&akid=5115%2E400544%2EQOVF8W)**
**Like many New Mexicans, I know what it’s like to struggle** — and I know what it takes to get back up and keep going. My experience as a working single mom fortified my resolve to build a better future for my child and every family fighting an uphill battle in our state and across the country.
From driving through New Mexico registering voters in rural towns to becoming one of the first Native women ever elected to Congress, every step of my journey has been possible because people like you believed in me. I’ll never stop fighting for our communities because I know that it takes a village — in life, and in politics.
Our campaign is fueled by grassroots donors who care about protecting our lands, uplifting working families, and making sure every voice is heard. **[That’s why I’m asking: will you chip in $5 to help us keep building a campaign powered by people, not special interests?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251017_1_singlemom.N0BOaB&amount=5&%3Brefcode=em20251017-5115&t=4&akid=5115%2E400544%2EQOVF8W)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251017_1_singlemom.N0BOaB&amount=5&refcode=em20251017-5115&t=23&akid=5115%2E400544%2EQOVF8W)**
Thank you for believing in me. With your grassroots support, we’re showing that anyone — including a single working mom with big dreams for New Mexico — can go up against billionaire politics and win.
Be fierce,
Deb

name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: What I heard from Americans living abroad in Berlin
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY POWERED BY PEOPLE
body:
[1]Powered By People

I recently had the chance to hold a town hall meeting with Democrats
Abroad in Berlin. I met Americans who love our country deeply—and who are
worried about the direction it’s heading in.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20251017.XW3nWs&refcode=ema20251017-240410&t=1002&akid=240410%2E444211%2EWTLLFL ]An image of Beto holding a microphone in front of a seated crowd. A
sign on the wall behind reads 'Democrats Abroad: Berlin Region'.

Julia was one of them, and I wanted to share with you what she said when
it was her turn with the mic:

“If I had to name a couple reasons why I feel like I can’t go back to
America, it would be affordable health care that I have here and
affordable child care; thank you very much, Berlin!”

She said she even feels guilty talking to friends back home—because the
things that make her life stable in Germany feel out of reach in America.

She’s right. These shouldn’t be privileges—they should just be human
rights.

We are the wealthiest, most powerful nation in the history of the world.
We have everything we need to make sure every American can see a doctor,

You’ve probably seen us all over the state lately, bringing _The Colorado Blueprint_ from Alamosa to Durango to Greeley to Grand Junction. Our Fight for Colorado tour has been a meaningful opportunity to do one of my very favorite things: meeting with and _really listening_ to Coloradans everywhere. All those conversations have brought us here.**[And today, I want to ask for just one thing: your endorsement of our plan. If you’re ready right now, I’d be honored to have your support>>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117489053/576648048/1558770408?refcode=em_WEI_PET_EndorseOurPlan_101725&&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMzJhMjdkMS1hMWFiLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=aJE2iexOd_CBHaCm-zjErmLXSLrAcwbRWs7D0o-eHOA=&emci=d2dfcb43-8aab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=132a27d1-a1ab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=51844520)** Our plan puts Coloradans front and center. These are just a few of the highlights:
1. **Standing up to Trump:** As the People’s Lawyer, I’ve taken every opportunity to stand up to this administration’s unlawful attacks. We’ve sued Trump 39 times (so far), and we’re winning in court. As Governor, I’ll keep up the relentless fight for our democracy.

2. **Protecting our land, air, and water:** If the federal government makes any move to sell off our irreplaceable public lands to the highest bidder, they’ll have to go through me. I will always fight for and protect our land, air, and water, continuing our transition to clean energy, developing proactive wildfire mitigation, reducing tailpipe emissions, and strengthening our oversight of air and water quality.

3. **Developing the opportunities our workforce deserves:** A call to service in ColoradoCorps, scaling access to quality training programs through zero-interest loans and living stipends, and a host of earn-and-learn programs will help more Coloradans access good jobs and living wages.

4. **Making homes and communities affordable:** We’ll boost the number of homes Coloradans can afford, protect renters from unfair practices, support first-time home-buyers, and so much more.

# **[The Hidden Tech Keeping AI From Collapse](https://substack.com/redirect/f0587c8d-d5f8-4545-a076-5ef0c17b18fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
AI is booming. But there's a growing problem no one wants to admit: **our infrastructure isn 't ready for it**.1
The U.S. grid is already stretched thin. In many states, it's decades overdue for upgrades. Now layer on thousands of energy-hungry AI data centers -- and it's a recipe for blackouts, water shortages, and failure.1
In fact, just this month, Bloomberg reported that AI data centers are **draining millions of gallons of water** from drought-prone areas in the U.S.9 Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is going the opposite direction -- investing **$100 billion** to build ultra-modern AI power hubs running on next-gen energy tech.
**The U.S. needs a breakthrough. That 's where [Next Thing Technologies](https://substack.com/redirect/f0587c8d-d5f8-4545-a076-5ef0c17b18fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) comes in.**
They're the first American company9 to develop a commercially-viable1 sodium-ion battery pack that can power AI infrastructure.1
Why it matters:
* Sodium is **1,400 × more abundant than lithium**9
* Batteries are projected to be **up to 60% cheaper** 6

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Things are tough right now—especially for people in Texas and across the country who are struggling with the many challenges brought by the government shutdown. People are worried about access to and the cost of healthcare, as well as the cost of just about everything else.
It is in moments like these that we must remember that we have the power to change things—and that each of us can do something to make that change.
One of those things is vote—and get other people to vote—for people and policies that will help, not hurt. That means working for candidates and sharing information with other voters about who you are supporting and why that matters. This campaign, this team effort, is a reminder that we can make that change.
And, with our work together in 2018, we made history. I was sworn in to the 116th Congress in January 2019 with some incredible people. People who, like me, were first time candidates, putting our names on the ballot because we knew that we deserved better from our government, and that we could help make it happen.
Now, two of my friends from the Class of 2018, Abigail Spanberger and Mikie Sherrill, are running for governor in critical elections in just a few weeks. These elections are absolutely vital—sending a message and sending two smart, dedicated, patriotic women to the governor’s offices in Virginia and New Jersey.
I have known and worked with Abigail and Mikie for years, and I know how lucky their states and the country will be to have them as governors. So, I hope you will join me in helping support them by participating in our TeamLizzie phonebanks for their campaigns.
📞 Join a virtual phonebank with Team Lizzie:
* Abigail Spanberger — Tuesday, October 22 @ 5 P.M. CT
( Abigail is the only Democrat in the country who can flip a governor’s seat blue this year. )
https://www.mobilize.us/spanbergerforgovernor/event/861456/ [https://www.mobilize.us/spanbergerforgovernor/event/861456/]
* Mikie Sherrill — Week of October 27
( Polls show this race is neck-and-neck, and we can help push Mikie across the finish line. )
https://forms.gle/xvfXQgHFJo8QqRuJ7 [https://forms.gle/xvfXQgHFJo8QqRuJ7]
Electing strong Democratic governors is one of the most powerful ways we can help stop President Trump and his administration’s authoritarian takeover of our government. With just 18 days until Election Day —and many people already voting early—we’re in a critical window.
And don’t forget: There are also important elections happening right here in Texas. Every single person in Texas will be asked to vote on amendments to the Texas Constitution. And voters all over the state will have other important races on the ballot.
Make your plan to vote:
* Early In-Person Voting in Texas Begins: Monday, October 20
* Last Day to Apply for a Mail Ballot in Texas: Friday, October 24 (must be received , not postmarked)
* Last Day of Early Voting in Texas: Friday, October 31
Find everything you need at: https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/index.shtml [https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/index.shtml]
Can’t volunteer right now? There are other ways to contribute:
* Forward this email to friends who might be able to volunteer—these phonebanks are virtual and can be done from anywhere
* Make a financial contribution [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/folfe251017?refcode=folfe251017] to our campaign—it is an investment in organizing in 2025 and winning in 2026, in Texas and across the country.
Let’s make these last 18 days count.
Together we can do anything,

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SPdTr5ah-NA [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SPdTr5ah-NA]
Friend,
Today, I joined with other local leaders to file a lawsuit against Tennessee Governor Bill Lee and his administration to stop the unlawful deployment of National Guard troops into Memphis.
Let me be clear: this action by the Governor, done at the request of the President, is not just wrong—it's illegal.
The Tennessee Constitution and state law are explicit. The Governor cannot unilaterally deploy the National Guard as a domestic police force without a request from local officials or a declaration from the legislature. He has neither.
You cannot enforce the law by breaking the law.
To see our city treated like a political pawn or a "training ground" is dangerous and dehumanizing. We have a crime problem that we must address with serious, community-based solutions—not by militarizing our streets in a move that usurps our local authority and intimidates our citizens.
This is not a partisan issue; it's a constitutional one. It’s about whether Memphis and Shelby County will be governed by our own elected leaders, or by politicians in Nashville and Washington, D.C.
I will always stand up for the people of Shelby County. Today, that means taking the Governor to court.
Join me in this fight. Send a clear message that we will not stand for this illegal overreach. Add your name to the "No Troops in Memphis" petition right now.

Trump and his allies have shut down the government.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117489857/576650765/623074613?refcode=jtk1422-fr-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTE4NmZiOWMtYTRhYi1mMDExLThlNjEtNjA0NWJkZWQ4YmE0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=kfd5tS-uGVRVVwV409a1IZN2NBTx9qcUoCz_eUXjD-k=&emci=a950b005-95ab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=1186fb9c-a4ab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=9329426)
---
Hello friend,

As we all know, this month the federal government came to a screeching halt. But let me make one thing clear: This is not a failure of the Democrats or government workers. This is a deliberate gambit on behalf of radical Republicans who are choosing to use the shutdown as a wrecking ball, to threaten irreversible cuts to healthcare, fire federal workers en masse, and destroy the programs that help keep their own constituents afloat.
While Trump and his allies try to shroud the truth, here’s the reality: **Premiums will skyrocket** , doubling or even tripling in many cases – squeezing normal working-class families beyond what their current paychecks can afford. My own constituents are not immune; our neighbors, coworkers, and even the veterans who serve our country will bear the brunt. We must make certain that **healthcare is no bargaining chip.**
But this doesn’t stop at insurance. **Connecticut is in the crosshairs, and Russell Vought is taking aim.** Unelected and a significant contributor to Project 2025, he is implementing a new regime of control deciding which programs live or die and which states are punished, with Democrat-led states being his biggest target. What is unfolding is a seizure of power masquerading as austerity, with numerous infrastructure, energy, and health projects being canceled or having their funds frozen. This, when coupled with his efforts to place federal workers “in trauma” through mass layoffs, is causing irreparable harm.
In 2024, Trump claimed he did not know this man or the other extremists behind Project 2025. But now we see that blueprint coming to life under a government run by ideology catering to itself and people just like them, not the people who elected it. Like the reckless cuts and chaos caused by Elon Musk and DOGE earlier this year, this administration is run by ego, not public service.
I am prepared to stand on the floor, speak to the media, and fight for what’s right to defend Connecticut and every American. We must fight for a democracy that serves every person under the flag, not just the power-hungry few.
If you believe that the government should serve the people, not the privileged, please chip in today, as every dollar helps us organize and build a movement needed to hold this administration accountable.

Dick

[1]Justice Democrats

The tide is turning against AIPAC,
Peter.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251017.0mEuxi&refcode=em20251017-37118&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37118%2E1203867%2EGfVHRf ]A headline from The New York Times reads 'Democrats Pull Away From
AIPAC, Reflecting a Broader Shift'. The subheading reads 'A quiet retreat
by Democrats from the pre-eminent pro-Israel lobbying group is the latest
evidence of a realignment underway in Congress on Israel.'

As our Communications Director, Usamah Andrabi, told the press this week:

“Our movement's work to demand the Democratic Party reject AIPAC as a
toxic pariah is not only working but ensuring that the pro-genocide Israel
lobby's influence in Washington is waning. AIPAC and its affiliated super
PACs—from the United Democracy Project to the Democratic Majority for
Israel—are transforming from a lobby that establishment Democrats could
rely on to buy a seat in Washington into a kiss of death for any candidate
who has their support."

The New York Times even said, “AIPAC is becoming an increasingly toxic
brand for some Democrats on Capitol Hill.” Here are just some of the
signs:

* Congressional Democrats who used to gladly count AIPAC as one of their
top campaign donors are now outright refusing their donations due to
public pressure.
* Fewer and fewer Democratic members are taking the annual
AIPAC-sponsored propaganda trip to Israel.
* A majority of the Senate Democratic Caucus has voted for bills to
block additional U.S. weapons sales to Israel, which AIPAC vehemently
opposes.

This is a turning point for the Democratic Party,
Peter, and with your support, Justice Democrats
helped usher it in. But the fight to fully reject AIPAC from the Party is
far from over, especially as we approach the 2026 primary elections.

We’ve already endorsed three anti-AIPAC, working-class, progressive
candidates to take on out-of-touch, corporate incumbents in next year’s
Democratic primaries, and we know AIPAC is likely to drop tens of millions
of dollars to try defeating them and unseating more members of the Squad
like they did last year.

It’s time to get back to work — now.

Peter,
Here are 3 quick things you should know about who I am and why I’m running to serve as California’s next governor:
1. One of my top priorities will be **standing up to Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans.** When Trump threatens Californians—whether it’s by withholding disaster aid or attacking our communities—I’ll always stand up to his bullying and fight back.

2. Our state faces real challenges. From housing and health care costs that are out of control, to a rapidly changing climate—we need new ideas and leaders with the backbone to fight for what’s right.

3. I held the first Trump Administration accountable in Congress and got real results **(sometimes with my whiteboard, sometimes without!)**. My questioning of Trump officials secured free COVID testing for every American in the earliest days of the pandemic, and I’m proud to have passed into law bills that hold Big Oil and Big Pharma accountable for ripping off taxpayers. [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117490879/576654803/693975070?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOWFlOTk1Ni1hYWFiLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=S_t1VSWy_etsX4Q4dNZPm5onTMo5sE3F3C5SoEyYSJM=&emci=6c203c88-8cab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=e9ae9956-aaab-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=15820338)
---
Peter,

Donald Trump is using this shutdown to _“clean house,"_ and his latest target is mental health and substance abuse programs that **millions** of Americans depend on.

Trump brushed off these mental health and addiction programs as “Democrat programs.” But for millions of families, they're not about politics—they're about survival. _Here's what these programs really mean:_

These programs connect parents and kids with therapy, school-based counseling, and crisis support. They fund treatment centers and community recovery programs that help people battling addiction. And they keep the 988 Lifeline and local crisis teams running, making sure there's always someone to answer the call when people need help most.

Cutting these programs isn't just cruel, **it's dangerous.**

It will cost lives, close clinics, and push struggling families even closer to the edge. This is what happens when self-serving extremists get power; they call care “partisan” and dismantle the very systems that keep Americans healthy and thriving, all while placing the blame on everyone else.

[**As a doctor, Kim knows these programs are vital, and they shouldn’t be put on the chopping block for political gain. clean_body: Donald Trump is using this shutdown to “clean house," and his latest target is mental health and substance abuse programs. Peter, Donald Trump is using this shutdown to “clean house," and his latest target is mental health and substance abuse programs that millions of Americans depend on. Trump brushed off these mental health and addiction programs as “Democrat programs.” But for millions of families, they're not about politics—they're about survival. Here's what these programs really mean: These programs connect parents and kids with therapy, school-based counseling, and crisis support. They fund treatment centers and community recovery programs that help people battling addiction. And they keep the 988 Lifeline and local crisis teams running, making sure there's always someone to answer the call when people need help most. Cutting these programs isn't just cruel, it's dangerous. It will cost lives, close clinics, and push struggling families even closer to the edge. clean_body: It’s the highlight of my day. | Would you pick up the phone if I called, Peter? This week, I made a few more phone calls to personally thank folks who’ve made grassroots donations to our campaign. I really love making these calls (and yes, I make them myself). I’ve had to convince a few people that it was not an A.I. call. One woman put me on speaker to talk with her family. One person told me she was a federal employee who had been furloughed. Another told me she loves her job as a school librarian. The list goes on! Since I enjoy it so much, I want to keep giving my supporters a ring. All you have to do is use this link to donate any amount, then leave your name and phone number to join the list of folks I could call: = Recently, I spoke with Barbara, Jim, and others about what their support means for us. I can tell you what I told them: We wouldn’t be able to do this without you. I’m more grateful than I can say every time someone steps up to give, and while I can’t call to say thank you to every single one of our supporters, I hope to get a few more phone calls in soon. There’s nothing that brings me more resolution — and enthusiasm — than talking with folks directly about this campaign and about our goals for this country. If you’d be interested in chatting, make a donation through the link below. Anything will count. = And don’t forget to leave your phone number! My regards, Roy Cooper = Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here. National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us. Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party. The White House is counting on them to be the latest batch of Republicans to flout the will of the people and kowtow to Trump’s redistricting power grab. It wasn’t that long ago in 2022 that Kansas lawmakers, including Republican Senate President Ty Masterson, promised not to split up the state’s Third Congressional District, which is represented by Kansas’s only Democrat, Sharice Davids. Hi, Derek,
I don’t think this is controversial: **If you make billions, you shouldn’t pay less in taxes than your secretary.** 🤷
But right now, that’s not how Trump’s tax law works. While people like nurses and firefighters pay taxes straight out of every paycheck, there’s a maze of shady rules and accounting tricks that let the billionaires walk away scot-free while the rest of us pay up.
That’s why I reintroduced the **Billionaires Income Tax Act** , legislation that would close loopholes and ensure billionaires pay their fair share in taxes.
Working Pennsylvanians already face high and rising prices, while billionaires and megacorporations game the system to pay next to nothing in taxes. **This bill is about basic fairness.** ⚖️

# **A Week Like Trump 's Hair: Very Fake & Fairly Flammable**
Some weeks the news doesn't just break, it tosses a Molotov cocktail and dares you to look away! This...was one of those weeks.
The show kicked off with a courtroom confrontation that could only happen in modern America.
ICE agents _were verbally demolished_ by a Jamaican-American woman in a New York courthouse after they snatched her relative. She lets them have it.
The full monty.
No filter, no apologies, an oral, rocket-propelled piss-missile of pure righteous fury.
The kind of real anger at an actual injustice. Unlike, say, [JD Vance fake and transparently absurd pretense he's a victim of the media](https://substack.com/redirect/9e139b74-49d0-4356-a2fd-72df349265ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or trans community, or 17-minute version of In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f6b025ee-d9c8-4344-a732-ad338a90420e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You can practically hear Lady Liberty slow-clapping from the harbor.
I mean, this woman didn't just speak truth to power; she _screamed_ it into their almost-always-masked, fear-factor f*king faces like a freedom-loving banshee.
I've seen plenty of passionate anger at the group of the deep-fried galoots known as ICE before, but this was some Shakespearean sh*t. A thing of beauty and so well deserved.
* * *
Support real journalists like David Shuster!
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.nnrb6zAn1G_9V6LLeDSmqTsed0B7sovqAROb8kUfI7A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=176448285)
* * *
Then, because we may not rest too long in the land of moral clarity, we tumble headfirst into the _Epstein files_. You know, the (alleged) Trump-teen-loving scandal that refuses to die, unlike farms owned by MAGA voters.
Trump calls it a "Democrat hoax," which is funny coming from a guy whose own party has more people sweating from this story than the Chinese spy and bed-bug-filled Mar-a-Lago sauna in August.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e139b74-49d0-4356-a2fd-72df349265ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Epstein victims are finally getting traction. Lobbying GOP lawmakers so effectively, that one Republican admitted the vote to release the files will be a "jailbreak."
**Translation:** expect some very nervous right-wingers to start pretending they've "always supported transparency." And when asked about Trump to say they met him once briefly, but don't really know him that well.
Meanwhile, Grindr spokesman and House Speaker [Mike Johnson is still blocking Adelita Grijalva, who was elected to Congress from Arizona nearly two weeks ago](https://substack.com/redirect/a6d645d6-e279-41fc-b8f7-c10221713e22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from being sworn into the House.
This is because she'll be the 218th signer--and final one the House needs--on a discharge petition to go around Squeaker Johnson and force a vote to release the Epstein files.
Little Mike's excuse? "She doesn't know how it works around here."
This is where we stop to tell the cowering, callow, fake-Christian pip-Speaker to do his GD job.
There are only so many cloak rooms to hide in to avoid this vote, pal. [Stop sabotaging your country.](https://substack.com/redirect/9560f810-bfb8-4839-9cf3-01933f9feb20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) A reckoning is coming.
* * *
Our message grows stronger with your backing
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.nnrb6zAn1G_9V6LLeDSmqTsed0B7sovqAROb8kUfI7A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=176448285)
* * *
Even Marjorie Taylor Greene, yes, _that_ _one_ , has found herself on the same side as Democrats. She is demanding truth and transparency around the Epstein files.
And supporting [opening the government and funding Obamacare subsidies](https://substack.com/redirect/8ba45986-ab95-4b5c-a46f-f90f94968889?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
When MTG becomes your moral compass you know you've entered the Tom Petty video for "Don't Come Around Here No More," or the story about that Alice lady it's based on.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/874197d5-b7e9-40b7-ba28-7f143a7659b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And just when [you think the GOP's moral basement has reached](https://substack.com/redirect/874197d5-b7e9-40b7-ba28-7f143a7659b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) seventh circle, we learn that there's still a Trump staffer hanging around the Administration who used to be in a group chat that literally called rape "epic."
Oh and praised Hitler. Yes, that very same one. The "Young Republicans" just might need a rebrand.
May I suggest "Future Defendants of America?" Or how about this, with their belief system, such as it is, maybe they skip in-between phases and just start taking video of their training sessions climbing monkey bars right now?
Ya know, [for the invasion of "war ravaged" Portland.](https://substack.com/redirect/e95d6c27-9e84-4db5-89a9-5922763c2ccf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In any case, we close with an AI remix of a Nazi-era tune-turned-Trump anthem, because why not?
If the world's on fire, we might as well sing a song together, my friends.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e139b74-49d0-4356-a2fd-72df349265ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Stay angry, stay amused, and as always--keep laughing through the madness.
**Schuster out.**

Trump calls it a "Democrat hoax," which is funny coming from a guy whose own party has more people sweating from this story than the Chinese spy and bed-bug-filled Mar-a-Lago sauna in August. | | ---|---|--- The Epstein victims are finally getting traction. Lobbying GOP lawmakers so effectively, that one Republican admitted the vote to release the files will be a "jailbreak." Translation: expect some very nervous right-wingers to start pretending they've "always supported transparency." And when asked about Trump to say they met him once briefly, but don't really know him that well. Meanwhile, Grindr spokesman and House Speaker , from being sworn into the House. This is because she'll be the 218th signer--and final one the House needs--on a discharge petition to go around Squeaker Johnson and force a vote to release the Epstein files. Little Mike's excuse? "She doesn't know how it works around here." This is where we stop to tell the cowering, callow, fake-Christian pip-Speaker to do his GD job. There are only so many cloak rooms to hide in to avoid this vote, pal. A reckoning is coming. Our message grows stronger with your backing Even Marjorie Taylor Greene, yes, that one , has found herself on the same side as Democrats. She is demanding truth and transparency around the Epstein files. And supporting . When MTG becomes your moral compass you know you've entered the Tom Petty video for "Don't Come Around Here No More," or the story about that Alice lady it's based on. | | ---|---|--- And just when seventh circle, we learn that there's still a Trump staffer hanging around the Administration who used to be in a group chat that literally called rape "epic." Oh and praised Hitler. Yes, that very same one. The "Young Republicans" just might need a rebrand. May I suggest "Future Defendants of America?" Or how about this, with their belief system, such as it is, maybe they skip in-between phases and just start taking video of their training sessions climbing monkey bars right now? Ya know, In any case, we close with an AI remix of a Nazi-era tune-turned-Trump anthem, because why not? If the world's on fire, we might as well sing a song together, my friends. | | ---|---|--- Stay angry, stay amused, and as always--keep laughing through the madness. Schuster out. This campaign isn’t about politics as usual, it’s about restoring common sense, accountability, and integrity in Washington.

**I’m running for Congress because I believe Arizona deserves leaders who still understand what service means. **

As a U.S. Army Veteran and a former Army chaplain candidate, I’ve seen what real leadership looks like and it’s not coming out of D.C. right now.

When I get to Washington, I will defend the Constitution, protect our families, secure our border, and bring back faith and responsibility to public service.
